description:
Turn a document the person already sends — their invoice, letterhead, minutes, a form — into a Galley template that reproduces its look, with a JSON Schema you can fill. PDF only (exported from the program that made it, not a scan), up to 10 pages and 20 MB.

**Getting the file to Galley — send exactly one:**
- `upload: true`, the usual answer in a chat. A file the person dropped into the conversation reaches you as pages to read, not as bytes you can pass on, so this returns a one-time upload link (15 minutes, one use) for the person and a curl line for an agent with a shell. Ask the person to open the link and drop the file; then call `get_import`.
- `file_url`, a public https link to the PDF (a share link the person pasted).
- `file_base64`, the bytes, up to 5 MB — only for a client that already holds them in code.

Then poll `get_import` every few seconds; an import is usually ready in a few minutes. Galley may ask up to three questions about what on the page is fixed and what changes (`get_import` shows each with an image of the region), `answer_import` answers them, and `save_import` makes the template once the person has seen the preview. Nothing is a template until it is saved.

Needs a verified account on a paid plan: the keyless trial cannot import (call `create_account` first), and Free answers `plan_required`. Each paid plan includes a number of imports a month, counted when one starts — failed and refused imports are not counted — and this answer says how many are left; nothing is billed per import. A document you import is sent to Anthropic's Claude API to be read and converted, under their 30-day retention; Galley deletes its copy within 7 days. Identity, financial and government documents (bank statements, diplomas, tax forms, tickets) are refused.

auto.description: Skip the questions: every one takes its recommended answer. Default false. Use it only when the person has said they do not want to be asked.

file_base64.description: The PDF's bytes, base64, at most 5 MB decoded. Only for a client that already holds the bytes in code. A model writing base64 out spends roughly a token for every two or three characters — a 100 KB PDF is tens of thousands of tokens — so in a chat use `upload: true`, and with a shell use its curl line.

file_url.description: A public https link to the PDF, such as a share link the person pasted. Fetched once, up to 20 MB, from public addresses only.

hint.description: What kind of document this is, if you know: `invoice`, `quote`, `meeting-minutes`, `letterhead`… A hint for the classifier, never a command; it does not change what the page says.

name.description: Name for the template this import will save as, e.g. `ashcroft-invoice`. Optional: save_import can name it too, and the draft proposes one.

upload.description: `true` for a one-time upload link (15 minutes, one use) to give the person, plus a curl line for an agent with a shell. The usual choice in a chat: a file someone dropped into the conversation reaches you as pages to read, not as bytes you can pass on. Send exactly one of `upload`, `file_url` and `file_base64`.

name: import_document
title: Make a template from a document the person already has
